This example represents ₹15,500 in gross revenue, not profit. Your actual earnings depend on how many clients you acquire, the time required for each job, and expenses such as printing, travel, hosting, taxes, and paid software.

Do not assume every customer will subscribe to monthly management. Many clients need only a one-time setup. Recurring revenue is possible when you provide an ongoing service that customers genuinely need and agree to pay for.

Step 6: Turn One-Time Projects into Recurring Services

Creating a QR code is often a one-time task. To earn repeat revenue, offer useful services that continue after delivery.

Possible monthly services include:

  • Updating a restaurant's menu and seasonal offers.
  • Refreshing promotional landing-page content.
  • Maintaining and testing the destination website.
  • Updating business contact or catalogue information.
  • Preparing new QR display artwork for campaigns.
  • Providing agreed reporting for feedback forms or supported analytics.

For example, a restaurant may pay a monthly fee if you regularly update its digital menu and promotional content. A shop running frequent campaigns may want new QR-linked offers every month.

Explain the monthly deliverables clearly. Do not charge a recurring fee for a static code that requires no ongoing work unless the client knowingly chooses a legitimate paid service with continuing benefits.

Static vs Dynamic QR Codes: What Should You Offer?

Understanding the difference between static and dynamic QR codes helps you select the right solution for each customer.

  • Static QR codes: The destination or encoded information is built into the code. They are useful for stable links and simple information. If the destination changes, you may need to create and redistribute a new code.
  • Dynamic QR codes: These typically use a redirect or management service so the destination can be changed without replacing the printed code. Features, scan analytics, pricing, and availability depend on the provider.

A free static QR code is often sufficient for a business with a permanent website or menu URL. Dynamic QR codes may be more appropriate when the owner needs to change destinations or measure scans, but check the provider's terms, pricing, and access requirements first.

Never promise that a code will remain editable forever unless the service terms support that claim. If a dynamic code depends on a paid platform, make sure the customer understands what happens if the subscription ends.

Step 7: Contact Clients with a Simple Sales Message

Keep your introduction short and focused on the customer's business. Avoid claiming that a QR code will automatically increase sales or guarantee more customers.

Here is an example you can adapt for a local cafe or restaurant:

Hello! I help local restaurants create simple digital menus that customers can open by scanning a QR code on their tables. I can prepare the menu link, generate and test the QR code, and design a ready-to-use table card. Would you be interested in seeing a quick sample for your restaurant?

For another business, adapt the offer to its needs. A salon might benefit from a service list and booking link, while a retailer might prefer a product catalogue or promotional page.

Listen to the owner's response before preparing a custom proposal. Agree on the scope and price before doing substantial unpaid work.

Step 8: Deliver a Professional QR Code Package

A professional delivery process helps you earn trust and encourages referrals.

For every client project:

  1. Confirm the destination URL and obtain approval from the business owner.
  2. Generate the QR code using an appropriate tool.
  3. Check colours, contrast, dimensions, and the quiet zone.
  4. Scan the code using more than one phone where possible.
  5. Test the destination on a mobile device and confirm that it loads correctly.
  6. Provide the agreed digital files and print-ready artwork.
  7. Explain how the customer can use the code and who will maintain the destination.
  8. Confirm delivery and collect payment according to the agreed terms.

For printed materials, use an appropriate file format and resolution. SVG is useful for scalable print artwork, while a sufficiently high-resolution PNG can work well for many digital and print applications. Always test a physical proof before ordering a large print run.

Can You Start This Business Without Investment?

You can start with very little upfront spending if you already have a computer or smartphone, internet access, and the skills to prepare the deliverables. A free QR code generator can eliminate the need to purchase QR creation software for basic projects.

However, some services may involve expenses. Printing, domain names, hosting, premium design tools, dynamic QR code subscriptions, paid form features, travel, and advertising can all add costs.

To keep your initial expenses low:

  • Start with simple QR codes linked to existing client pages.
  • Use free design tools where their terms permit commercial use.
  • Ask the client to pay for printing or other third-party expenses separately.
  • Avoid buying subscriptions before you have a real client requirement.
  • Keep written records of the price, deliverables, and payment terms.

The most important early investment is often your time: learning the workflow, creating a good sample, identifying potential customers, and delivering reliable work.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Selling only the code: A customer can often generate a basic QR code independently. Offer a useful finished solution instead.
  • Failing to test: A code that opens the wrong page or fails to scan can damage your reputation. Test before delivery.
  • Using unreliable destinations: Confirm that the linked menu, form, or website is accessible to the intended audience.
  • Ignoring ownership: Use the client's approved content and agree on ownership and access to accounts or landing pages.
  • Promising permanent service without checking terms: A free generator does not necessarily provide free hosting, editable destinations, or analytics.
  • Printing without a proof: Check the final physical size, contrast, margins, and scan performance before producing many copies.
  • Expecting guaranteed income: Revenue depends on finding customers and delivering a service they value. Start small and measure your results.

Your First 7-Day Action Plan

If you want to test this business idea, follow a manageable one-week plan.

  • Day 1: Learn how to generate, download, and test different types of QR codes.
  • Day 2: Create a sample digital menu and a sample feedback-form QR card.
  • Day 3: Choose one service package and write down exactly what it includes.
  • Day 4: Find 15–20 relevant local businesses and identify their potential needs.
  • Day 5: Contact a small number of businesses with personalised messages or visit them in person.
  • Day 6: Follow up with interested prospects and prepare clear quotes.
  • Day 7: Review responses, improve your sample, and plan the next round of outreach.

These steps are a starting plan, not a guarantee of acquiring a client within seven days. Keep track of your outreach and learn which services attract genuine interest.

Start with one straightforward service, such as a digital menu, a customer feedback form, or a branded business contact QR code. Build a working sample, approach relevant businesses, and improve your offer based on their feedback.

When you are ready to create your first code, visit the TechMind.click Free QR Code Generator. Generate your code, test it, and prepare a professional deliverable that solves a real problem for your client.

Remember: the QR code is the tool. The value you provide through design, setup, convenience, and ongoing support is what turns it into a service business.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can I sell QR codes created with a free generator?

Generally, you can charge for your own design, setup, and delivery services when the tool's terms permit commercial use. Check the specific generator's licence and terms, especially for logos, branding, premium features, and redistribution.

Do I need to create my own QR code generator?

No. You can begin with an existing free generator. Building your own software is only necessary if you want to offer a specialised platform or features that existing tools do not provide.

Can I earn monthly income from QR codes?

Potentially. You can offer monthly menu updates, landing-page maintenance, campaign support, or dynamic QR code management. Recurring income depends on retaining paying clients and providing services they continue to need.

Do free QR codes expire?

A standard static QR code generally does not expire on its own, but the destination can stop working if the website or linked content is removed. Dynamic codes may depend on the provider's subscription and terms.

How much should I charge a local business?

Pricing depends on your work and the local market. You might charge a few hundred rupees for a basic code and more for a branded design, menu setup, feedback form, or landing page. Explain the deliverables and agree on the price before beginning.

How do I get my first QR code customer?

Create a demonstration, identify businesses with a relevant need, and contact them with a personalised offer. Showing a working sample is often more useful than simply telling an owner that you sell QR codes.

Can I use a QR code to collect payments or donations?

Yes, where the payment provider supports the intended use. Use an approved payment link or payment QR code, verify the recipient details, and follow the provider's rules and applicable requirements. Never redirect customer payments to an account without the business owner's authorisation.
